name: Shishak
bio: Shishak was king of Egypt. When Solomon sought to kill his official Jeroboam after the prophet Ahijah announced that Jeroboam would receive ten tribes of the kingdom, Jeroboam fled to Shishak's Egypt and remained there in exile until Solomon's death (1 Kings 11:40). In the fifth year of Rehoboam's reign, Shishak marched against Jerusalem and carried off the treasures of both the temple and the royal palace, including all the gold shields Solomon had made (1 Kings 14:25-26). Chronicles gives the scale of his invasion in detail: 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen, and countless troops of Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites, who captured Judah's fortified cities before reaching Jerusalem itself. The prophet Shemaiah told Rehoboam and Judah's leaders that the LORD had allowed this because they had abandoned him; when they humbled themselves in response, the LORD spared Jerusalem from complete destruction through Shishak, though Judah would still become his subjects for a time (2 Chronicles 12:1-9).
